messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] p99 streaming tail latency spike in eu-west2 detected at 2026-03-15T08:02:23Z. p99=1100ms (SLO=300ms), p95=450ms. Error rate for streaming sessions +2.3%. Auto-page to #incidents-oncall. 
jen: paging oncall. I'm oncall, grabbing it. gathering initial telemetry. 
sam: copying graphs — p99 jump aligns with 08:01:40-08:02:10 window. DNS failure spikes seen from eu-west2 private NATs. 
maria: @sam can you paste the DNS error logs? suspecting cross-zone NAT flaps after recent routing push. 
sam: logs:
```
[08:01:42] resolver.go: failed lookup host "model-service.internal": i/o timeout
[08:01:43] nat-proxy: conn reset by peer
[08:01:44] tls: handshake timeout
```
ash: screenshots of Cloud NAT metrics: connection count stayed steady but ephemeral port exhaustion flared for ~30s across az-b. high SYN retransmits to 52.23.10.0/24. 
dan: are we seeing packet loss or just handshake delays? 
emily: client-side retransmits + increased RTOs in tcpdump capture. packet loss ~1.8% at egress path, small but enough to blow up TLS p99. 
jen: impact: streaming tail stalls for ~700-1200ms for ~4% of active streams. Some customers with low-latency SLOs will see degraded UX. No wide customer disconnects reported yet. 
sam: routing table change rolled out 07:58 across eu-west2 (route-optimizer v2). rolling back may help but needs coordination. 
maria: agreeing — suspect route-optimizer introduced asymmetric path hitting overloaded NAT cluster. recommend immediate traffic steering to alternate egress for eu-west2 az-b. 
jen: mitigation plan: 1) divert traffic from az-b NAT to az-a (steer via BGP weight change), 2) enable temporary ip-masq reuse on NAT proxies, 3) increase TLS handshake timeout fallback to reduce client error noise. 
nash: executing BGP weight bump now for asg-eu-west2-azb -> bump +50. 
incident-bot: deploybot: route-optimizer rollback initiated by @sam at 08:04:12Z. CI checks green, rolling rollback to 07:50 snapshot. 
sam: rollback in progress — stage 1 complete, stage 2 starting (target 10 nodes). expect stabilization in ~90s. 
emily: packetloss metric already trending down after BGP adjustment. p95 improving. 
jen: status update to customers: draft message ready. short note about "transient latency affecting streaming; mitigations in progress; no data loss". @ash can you sign off on wording? 
ash: lgtm. send from status.redwood.com, include timeframe and recommended retry behavior. 
dan: verifying streaming gateway logs — KV cache misses spiked during handshake failures but recovered. no token or auth errors. 
maria: NAT ephemeral reuse toggled to 1s TTL to avoid port churn. will monitor. 
sam: rollback finished at 08:06:20Z. p99 now at 270ms. 
jen: excellent. declaring mitigation successful. moving to post-incident triage. 
incident-bot: incident status -> mitigated. Runbook: oncall followup required. 
jen: actions: 1) reopen routing rollout playbook, 2) investigate route-optimizer change that introduced asymmetry, 3) add NAT ephemeral port headroom to autoscaler, 4) add alert to detect small packet loss-induced TLS tail spikes. assign owners: @maria for routing, @ash for NAT autoscaler, @sam for route-optimizer code, @emily for observability alerts. 
maria: starting forensic capture of BGP adj changes and flow logs; will attach to triage doc. 
emily: I'll add a p99-by-az dashboard and alert (threshold 400ms) and a streaming-tail correlation panel with TLS handshake failures & DNS timeouts. 
jen: schedule blameless postmortem tomorrow 09:30 UTC. 
ash: quick note: recommend customers using strict 100ms TLS timeouts adopt exponential backoff; ops doc to be published. 
jen: thanks team. I'll update the incident ticket and notify affected accounts with the draft. closing thread here; please update triage doc with artifacts. :white_check_mark:
